File: /root/.claude/projects/-ai-inventor/memory/project_qwen3_safety_genplan_exp1_iter2_run_fcYd.md

---
name: project-qwen3-safety-genplan-exp1-iter2-run-fcyd
description: "Iter2 GEN_PLAN experiment_1 (readout bake-off + family panel + LOFO race) run_fcYd_7ruOwtm — the direction's PART ordering is a narration order, not an execution order: the harvest feeds BOTH parts and must run first; and the 0.391 below-chance AUROC may be a DEGENERATE BASE RATE, not a broken readout"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

Run `run_fcYd_7ruOwtm` iter_2 `gen_plan_experiment_1` = artifact direction `experiment_iter2_dir3`
(repair the refusal readout, then buy the FAMILY axis). Sole dep = research `art_DeogIL_xh3pE`
(incumbent specs). Siblings planned in parallel: experiment_2, experiment_3, evaluation_1.
See [[project-qwen3-safety-genstrat-iter2-run-fcyd]] for what iteration 1 actually left behind.

## THE ORDERING TRAP IN THE DIRECTION ITSELF
The direction says "PART 1 the readout bake-off, PART 2 the family panel, PART 3 the race" and an
executor that follows that literally will try to bake off readouts before it has any activations or
generations to read. **The harvest is the shared substrate for BOTH parts**, exactly as iter-1's
strategy intended ("design the harvest first, then ask which candidates it already pays for").
⇒ Execution order is: precheck -> harvest -> BARRIER -> bake-off -> race. The bake-off's
pre-registration (definitions, acceptance bar, invariance bar, tiebreak) is written and HASHED
before the harvest, which is what makes it a bake-off rather than a post-hoc pick.

## THE FIX THAT KEEPS THE FROZEN REGISTRY VALID
The 50 metrics ship with a sha256 and must be reused UNCHANGED, but the across-item metrics are all
built on a refusal-drive function the bake-off is about to replace. Editing the registry would break
the hash; picking a readout after seeing the race would be tuning.
**Resolution: the registry is PARAMETRIC over R(.). Compute every R-dependent metric under ALL
THREE readouts, record the choice in a separate `readout_choice.json`, report the chosen R as
primary and the other two as sensitivity columns.** Hash stays valid; the reader can see whether the
verdict depends on the readout. Reuse this whenever a frozen artifact depends on a primitive a later
iteration has to repair.

## THE DIAGNOSIS THE DIRECTION DID NOT CONSIDER — CHECK IT BEFORE BLAMING THE READOUT
Iter-1's refusal-drive vs judged-refusal AUROC was 0.750 on Qwen3-4B and **0.391 on its abliterated
sibling**. Below chance reads as a broken readout, but an abliterated model may refuse ~0 of the
items, in which case the LABEL is degenerate and AUROC is unstable rather than inverted.
⇒ Pre-register: if the judged-refusal base rate is <5% or >95% on a checkpoint, report AUROC as
UNDEFINED with the base rate printed. That is a different and more honest finding than "the readout
failed", and it costs nothing to check.

## THE NESTED-SELECTION LEAK, AND WHY IT IS FREE TO CLOSE HERE
Selecting the readout on the same checkpoints the LOFO race scores is tuning on the test set. Since
all three readouts are computed for every checkpoint anyway, **re-run the race with R re-selected
INSIDE each leave-one-family-out fold** and report both tables. Costs one extra scoring pass, no
extra GPU. Same trick applies to any "we picked the best variant then evaluated it" pipeline.

## THE FOUR-DATASET ROW DESIGN (the exp_gen_sol_out contract forces this decision FIRST)
D1 readout_bakeoff (ckpt,item,presentation) -> predict_logitgap/refmass/greedy24
D2 family_race (metric_id,ckpt) -> predict_lofo/tuned/anisonull/lexfloor/familyonly, fold=family idx
D3 prompt_budget (ckpt,k,seed) -> predict_internal/predict_blackbox
D4 poles (pole_ckpt,metric_id) -> predict_level/spread/verdict
Everything that is not a per-example prediction (AUROC tables, CIs, permutation p, crossover point,
gate branches) goes in a separate free-form `analysis_out.json`.
**Definition (iii), the 24-token greedy continuation, SHARES ITS GRADER with the target, so it is
favoured by construction** — say so and print its judge-token cost beside its AUROC, because that
cost is exactly the "few prompts at most" constraint the whole request is about.

## THE SHRINK ORDER, PRE-COMMITTED (so it is not decided under time pressure)
Keep: arch precheck table, bake-off, two-way LOFO race + its three baseline columns, the poles.
Drop first: nested-selection second race, three-way race, k=64, paraphrase/translated conditions,
2000-resample bootstrap (-> 500).
**Never drop: the anisotropy-matched null, the MATCHED lexical floor, the family-label-only
baseline, the harvest barrier.** Those four are what make any number mean anything.

**How to apply:** when a direction narrates parts in dependency-violating order, re-derive the true
execution DAG from what each part consumes, and say so in the plan — the executor follows the plan,
not the direction.
```

# SEALED FOR ITERATION 2

Drawn with the fixed seed 20260920 and touched by NOTHING in this artifact.
The loader raises on any sealed repo (`screen/panel.sealed_guard`).

## Sealed model families (2)
- Granite
- StableLM2

Concretely: ibm-granite/granite-3.2-2b-instruct, stabilityai/stablelm-2-1_6b-chat

These two families are NEVER downloaded, NEVER harvested, and appear in no
output file other than this one and the `sealed_not_touched` list in
`results/panel_dropped.json`. They are the held-out validation panel for
whichever candidate iteration 2 promotes.

## Item fold 4 -- what is and is NOT true of it

Stated precisely, because the weaker claim is the true one: fold
4 is used in this artifact, as one of the five out-of-fold
EVALUATION folds. It is not untouched data.

What IS true is that no direction, layer, coordinate or threshold is ever
CHOSEN using it: every fitted direction is fitted on the other four folds and
scored only out-of-fold. So fold 4 carries no selection
leakage, but it is not a fresh confirmation split, and iteration 2 should not
treat it as one. The genuine seal in this artifact is the family seal above.

## B. Latest stable transformers release (as of 2026‑09) and breaking changes

- **Latest stable: `5.17.0`, released 2026‑09‑09** (recent train: 5.16.1 Aug 26 → 5.16.0 Aug 26 → 5.15.1 Aug 19 → 5.15.0 Aug 10 → 5.14.x Jul). Source: PyPI release history via [pypi.org/project/transformers](https://pypi.org/project/transformers/). Requires Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.5+.
- **`transformers` v5.0.0** (the major-version break) shipped **2026‑01‑26**. Source: [v5.0.0 release](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases/tag/v5.0.0), [MIGRATION_GUIDE_V5.md](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/MIGRATION_GUIDE_V5.md).
- **Breaking changes relevant to you:**
  1. **`torch_dtype` → `dtype`**: deprecated in **4.56** (PR #39782), `dtype` is now the correct kwarg. In v5, `torch_dtype` still exists as a deprecated alias per multiple ecosystem PRs (pruna, vllm, diffusers all switched to `dtype` to kill warnings around 4.56+), but you should write your harvester with `dtype=torch.bfloat16` going forward and only fall back to `torch_dtype=` for transformers <4.56.
  2. **`dtype` default changed to `"auto"` in v5**: previously `from_pretrained` defaulted to float32 unless you passed a dtype; in v5 the default became `"auto"` (load in the checkpoint's saved dtype). This is called out as one of the "three changes most likely to break your code immediately" (silent numerical drift) — **you must explicitly pass `dtype=torch.bfloat16` and not rely on defaults**, doubly so since your experiment cares about bf16 specifically.
  3. **`output_hidden_states=True` prefill**: I could not find a documented v5-specific behavior change to hidden-state output on prefill/generate in the migration guide or GitHub issues — this remains governed by longstanding, still-open issues (e.g. #29839, #28413, #36636) where `generate()` truncates/omits intermediate hidden states; if your harvest needs full-sequence hidden states, call the **forward pass directly** (`model(**inputs, output_hidden_states=True)`) rather than `.generate()`, which is unaffected by this ambiguity and is the documented-safe path in every version I could verify.
  4. **`apply_chat_template(..., enable_thinking=False)` for Qwen3**: works as documented, but note **[GitHub issue #38871](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/38871) "Qwen3 thinking flag is flipped"** — there was a real bug where the flag's polarity was inverted in some transformers version; verify empirically on your pinned version (print the templated string and check for a `<think>` tag) rather than trusting the flag blindly. Also `apply_chat_template` by default now returns a `BatchEncoding` dict rather than naked `input_ids` per the v5 migration guide — if you call it with `tokenize=True` (default), adjust code expecting a bare tensor.
  5. **`attn_implementation="eager"` for gemma‑2 soft‑capping**: still needed. Soft‑capping is incompatible with SDPA/FlashAttention at the kernel level (upstream limitation, not a version-fixed bug); Google's own gemma‑2 model card recommends `eager` for both correctness and stable fine-tuning. This has **not** changed by v5.17 — no evidence any current attention backend supports gemma‑2's exact soft-cap math besides `eager` (some third-party TransformerEngine FA2/FA3 forks added it, but that's not in vanilla `transformers`).
  6. **`AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., attn_implementation=...)`**: **yes, still supported in v5.17**. The attention-interface refactor (`attention_interface.py`) kept `attn_implementation` as the primary supported kwarg; only `use_flash_attention_2=True` (the old boolean shortcut) is deprecated in favor of `attn_implementation="flash_attention_2"`. Backends: `eager`, `sdpa`, `flash_attention_2`, `flash_attention_3`, `flex_attention`, plus paged variants.
  7. Also from the v5 migration guide, unrelated but worth flagging if your scripts touch it: TF/JAX backends fully removed, HTTP backend switched `requests`→`httpx` (catch `httpx.HTTPError` not `requests.HTTPError`), `AutoFeatureExtractor` deprecated for `AutoImageProcessor`.

MINIMUM VERSION PER ARCHITECTURE (sourced from the release notes, not guessed): llama ~4.28 ·
qwen2 4.37 · stablelm 4.38 · phi3 4.41 · gemma2 4.42 · granite ~4.44 · olmo2 4.47 ·
gemma3_text 4.50 (it was ONLY on the special `v4.49.0-Gemma-3` git tag, never in the 4.49 PyPI
wheel) · qwen3 4.51 (below it you get `KeyError: 'qwen3'`) · smollm3 4.53.
=> THE 4.x FLOOR FOR THIS PANEL IS 4.53.0, and 4.55-4.57 is the safe 4.x band.
`minicpm` IS NOT NATIVE AT ANY VERSION — there is no models/minicpm in transformers; it ships its
own modeling file and needs trust_remote_code=True. If the harvester forbids trust_remote_code
(it should), MiniCPM is DROPPED, not version-pinned. Granite-4.0's hybrid `granite-4.0-h-*`
variants need >= 5.8; only the plain dense `granite-4.0-micro` is safe — and Granite is SEALED
here anyway.
LATEST STABLE IS 5.17.0 (2026-09-09); v5.0.0 broke compatibility on 2026-01-26. FOUR v5 CHANGES
THAT WILL SILENTLY CORRUPT THIS EXPERIMENT IF IGNORED:
  (a) `torch_dtype` was deprecated in 4.56 in favour of `dtype`, AND THE DEFAULT CHANGED: in v5,
      from_pretrained defaults to `dtype="auto"` (the checkpoint's saved dtype) where 4.x defaulted
      to float32. THIS STUDY IS ABOUT bf16-AS-SHIPPED, so PASS `dtype=torch.bfloat16` EXPLICITLY
      AND NEVER RELY ON THE DEFAULT. Silent numerical drift here would contaminate every level
      metric, and the panel already mixes float16 (venkycs SmolLM2) and float32 (OLMo-2-0425-1B,
      mlabonne Qwen3-4B-abliterated) checkpoints — report magnitude statistics PER DTYPE.
  (b) `generate()` TRUNCATES OR OMITS INTERMEDIATE HIDDEN STATES (long-standing issues #29839,
      #28413, #36636). DO NOT read h_first out of a generation call. Get the first-content-token
      hidden states from a DIRECT FORWARD PASS on prompt+generated-prefix
      (`model(**inputs, output_hidden_states=True)`), which is the documented-safe path at every
      version. This is a correctness bug waiting to happen in stage B3 as I first wrote it.
  (c) THE Qwen3 THINKING FLAG'S POLARITY WAS INVERTED IN AT LEAST ONE RELEASE
      (github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/38871). DO NOT TRUST `enable_thinking=False`
      ON THE FLAG ALONE. PRINT THE TEMPLATED STRING and assert no `<think>` tag is present, for
      every Qwen3 checkpoint, at the pinned version. Combined with the B3 first-token assertion
      this gives two independent checks on the single trap this whole artifact was commissioned
      to rule out. Also: `apply_chat_template` with the default `tokenize=True` now returns a
      BatchEncoding dict, not a bare tensor — code expecting `input_ids` directly will break.
  (d) v5 switched the HTTP backend from `requests` to `httpx`; catch `httpx.HTTPError`, not
      `requests.HTTPError`. TF and JAX backends are gone.
`attn_implementation=` IS still supported in 5.17 (eager / sdpa / flash_attention_2 /
flash_attention_3 / flex_attention); only the old boolean `use_flash_attention_2=True` is
deprecated. gemma-2 soft-capping still REQUIRES eager — that is an upstream kernel limitation, not
a bug that any version fixed.

ACCESS STATES RE-CHECKED THIS WEEK, and three are newly broken. `huihui-ai/Qwen3-4B-abliterated`
returns 200 with gated:"auto" ANONYMOUSLY but iteration 1 recorded a hard 403 WITH auth — treat it
as unreachable and keep DreamFast/qwen3-4b-heretic + mlabonne/Qwen3-4B-abliterated as the Qwen3
abliterated arms (both already harvested). THREE huihui-ai repos now return a reproducible 401 to
anonymous access from both the REST API and the web page:
`huihui-ai/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-abliterated`, `huihui-ai/Phi-4-mini-instruct-abliterated`,
`huihui-ai/Huihui-SmolLM3-3B-abliterated`. That is a genuine access-control state, not a fetch
artifact. RE-CHECK EACH WITH THE TOKEN AT EXECUTION TIME
(`curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" https://huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>`) before
scheduling them, and fall back to the panel.py ids that iteration 1 already resolved:
lunahr/Phi-4-mini-instruct-abliterated and
Goekdeniz-Guelmez/Josiefied-Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-abliterated-v1.
FAMILIES WITH NO SAFETENSORS ABLITERATED SIBLING AT ALL — state this as a finding rather than
hunting: OLMo-2 (none exists), SmolLM2 (only a GGUF mirror, disqualified by the never-GGUF rule),
granite-4.0 (too new). Those families enter the panel INSTRUCT-ONLY and contribute to the
standalone-checkpoint arm the request explicitly asked for ("standalone models where no sibling
exists at all"), not to the two-way race. Say so in the table rather than quietly dropping them.
gemma-2's abliterated sibling is `IlyaGusev/gemma-2-2b-it-abliterated` (ungated, verified) —
huihui-ai has no gemma-2-2b-it abliteration.

Compute every R-dependent metric under ALL\nTHREE readouts, record the choice in a separate `readout_choice.json`, report the chosen R as\nprimary and the other two as sensitivity columns.** Hash stays valid; the reader can see whether the\nverdict depends on the readout. Below chance reads as a broken readout, but an abliterated model may refuse ~0 of the\nitems, in which case the LABEL is degenerate and AUROC is unstable rather than inverted.\n⇒ Pre-register: if the judged-refusal base rate is <5% or >95% on a checkpoint, report AUROC as\nUNDEFINED with the base rate printed. That is a different and more honest finding than \"the readout\nfailed\", and it costs nothing to check.\n\n## THE NESTED-SELECTION LEAK, AND WHY IT IS FREE TO CLOSE HERE\nSelecting the readout on the same checkpoints the LOFO race scores is tuning on the test set. Since\nall three readouts are computed for every checkpoint anyway, **re-run the race with R re-selected\nINSIDE each leave-one-family-out fold** and report both tables. Costs one extra scoring pass, no\nextra GPU. (ckpt,item,presentation) -> predict_logitgap/refmass/greedy24\nD2 family_race (metric_id,ckpt) -> predict_lofo/tuned/anisonull/lexfloor/familyonly, fold=family idx\nD3 prompt_budget (ckpt,k,seed) -> predict_internal/predict_blackbox\nD4 poles (pole_ckpt,metric_id) -> predict_level/spread/verdict\nEverything that is not a per-example prediction (AUROC tables, CIs, permutation p, crossover point,\ngate branches) goes in a separate free-form `analysis_out.json`.\n**Definition (iii), the 24-token greedy continuation, SHARES ITS GRADER with the target, so it is\nfavoured by construction** — say so and print its judge-token cost beside its AUROC, because that\ncost is exactly the \"few prompts at most\" constraint the whole request is about.\n\n## THE SHRINK ORDER, PRE-COMMITTED (so it Refusal-token mass is uncomputable from it, so the schema must be extended and only the 6 bake-off checkpoints re-harvested; the other 11 are inherited unchanged.

- **Three v5 traps that would silently corrupt results**: `dtype` now defaults to `"auto"` (not fp32), `generate()` truncates intermediate hidden states, and the Qwen3 `enable_thinking` flag's polarity was inverted in at least one release — so the plan asserts on the *templated string*, not the flag.
- **The frozen registry's `predicted_gap_rank` is not the hypothesis's ordering.** It puts behaviour-structure at the *smallest* gap, ahead of across-item. The plan scores that frozen ordering and says so, rather than substituting the headline's simpler level-vs-across-item split.
- **Iteration 1's null was upward-biased** (a max over 20 draws), which is why it tied the fitted probe at 0.921. Replaced with a B=1000 distribution in three tiers, with the sign fixed on train folds.
